caveats: All runs: direct-read mode (HOMEPROV_READ=direct) on an image built from a pinned copy of monitor/monitor.py sha256 8ad9e2d77f2d098af1e81ed509445631dc3d3ba2d349fddff75bfd920a7ab8ae (checked in the image), which carries the direct-read lock fix (E9_IMPL_NOTES.md section 11.0: validate_files() runs before the read connection is opened and after it is closed, never while the read is held; while it is held the WAL header's checkpoint sequence and salts and the database's change counter are compared through descriptors opened before and closed after the connection, and a change fails the read as read_raced) and the security re-check N2 (a raced direct read is retried, up to DIRECT_READ_ATTEMPTS reads per poll; read_attempts_counts counts the reads per measured poll).

Same synthetic recorders (masters k1, k5, k15, unchanged sha256), the same Docker limits on the monitor container, the same 30 measured polls after 3 warm-up polls at a 5 s period, the same writer (the recorder's own rows of one day earlier, one transaction per second) and the same monitor environment as exp/out/e9_cost_scale.json (stable scheme, coverage, keylog, escrow, Ed25519 signatures, tagged replies; HOMEPROV_ROWBIND and HOMEPROV_NAMEMAP_DIR not set), so the two files compare; only the monitor code differs.

Two quick_check cadences: HOMEPROV_QUICK_CHECK_EVERY=1 (the default, every poll) and 720 (once per hour at 5 s polls, which within 33 polls is the first, warm-up poll only). quick_check_outcomes counts, per run, the measured polls on which quick_check ran and passed or failed (recorded by a timing wrapper around monitor.check_connection; the warm-up polls are listed separately).

wal_bytes: the live recorder's -wal file size, sampled before and after every poll (series_after_poll for the 30 measured polls). The WAL file is not truncated by a passive checkpoint, so its size is the furthest the writer has extended it; it grows past the autocheckpoint size (1000 pages, the default the writer keeps, as the recorder does) when backfill is held off, e.g. by a read transaction held during quick_check. reference_wal_runs gives the same series for the copy-mode runs of exp/out/e9_cost_scale.json at the same sizes and writer load, where no read is held on the live recorder.
Observable = a poll that sealed (not evidence_unobservable); unobservable_reasons counts the fail-closed reasons, including read_raced.
rows_in_open_window differs between runs because the monitor re-reads from the start of the previous hour and longer runs cross an hour boundary; load and commit times scale with it.

Storage reads are cache misses only; the 1 GB memory limit of the monitor container bounds its cache and pages the writer touched may be served from the VM's cache; proc_rchar counts the bytes read through system calls whether cached or not.

Runs were made after the E2 night driver finished (its 2026-10-10 driver_done line); the Mac was otherwise shared, and load averages and per-container CPU at the start, every 300 s and at the end of each run are in runs[*].steps.

definitions.total: wall time of monitor.tick() for one poll (everything the poll does)
definitions.phase_*: time inside that monitor function during the poll (timers only; nested calls counted in both, e.g. watermark inside keylog_poll is not nested, validate_copy holds quick_check)
definitions.proc_read_bytes/write_bytes: from /proc/self/io: bytes the monitor process caused to be fetched from / sent to storage in the poll (page-cache hits are not reads)
definitions.proc_rchar/wchar: bytes passed through read/write-type system calls (includes page-cache hits)
definitions.cgroup_rbytes/wbytes: the container's cgroup io.stat on the VM disk (includes writeback)
definitions.bytes_written_per_hour: sum over the measured polls / the measured window's seconds * 3600: the run's measured rate, expressed per hour

reference_wal_runs.what: the live -wal size in earlier runs of exp/out/e9_cost_scale.json at the same sizes and writer load (copy mode reads a copy, so no read is held on the live recorder): a baseline for the WAL growth without a direct read
